title: Personal Credit Cards: how many points a closing cash-out takes and their cash value
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: size and value of a closing points cash-out

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder who is closing a card asks to cash out its rewards points into an active PCB checking account, it fixes how many points are cashed out and the cash they are worth.

## Rule

1. All of the card's unredeemed points are redeemed as one deposit-to-checking redemption; the cash-out is not split and is not partial.
2. When the unredeemed points are below the tier's smallest redemption, no deposit is made either, and the points cashed out are 0.
3. The cash value is the points multiplied by the tier's cash value per point, rounded half-up to the cent.
4. The tier's travel value per point never applies to a deposit.

## Truth table

| Unredeemed points at least the smallest redemption | Points cashed out | Cash value |
|---|---|---|
| yes | all unredeemed points, in one deposit | points multiplied by the cash value per point, rounded half-up |
| no | 0 | none |

## Worked examples (hypothetical terms: smallest redemption 1000 points, cash value 0.03 USD, travel value 0.05 USD per point)

| Unredeemed points | Points cashed out | Cash value |
|---|---|---|
| 6600 | 6600 | 198.00 USD, at the cash value, never at the travel value |
| 1000 | 1000 | 30.00 USD |
| 800 | 0 | no deposit |

## Wrong reading and correct basis

- **Wrong:** cash out only the part of the points the cardholder wants and leave the rest. **Correct:** all unredeemed points are cashed out in one deposit.
- **Wrong:** value the points at the travel value because the tier has one. **Correct:** a deposit is valued at the cash value per point.
